metadata.title: Random But True: The Wallpaper Nobody Wanted That Changed Shipping
metadata.caption:
1957, Hawthorne, New Jersey. Engineers Al Fielding and Marc Chavannes sealed two plastic shower curtains together, trapping tiny pockets of air - trying to invent a textured 3D wallpaper.

Nobody wanted it. It flopped completely. They tried again as greenhouse insulation. That flopped too.

In 1960 they founded a company anyway - Sealed Air - still without a real use for the material. Then a Sealed Air marketer realized the bubbles were perfect for protecting fragile items in shipping, and pitched it to IBM for their computers.

IBM said yes. That one pitch turned a failed wallpaper into one of the most recognized packaging materials on Earth - and Sealed Air Corporation still makes it today.

It was invented to be looked at. It got famous for being popped instead.
